Cabinet approves 29 public holidays for 2027
item.description:
The cabinet has approved 29 public holidays for 2027, including 15 general holidays and 14 holidays declared by executive order, with 22 effective holidays after excluding those coinciding with weekly weekends.
The decision was taken at the 26th cabinet meeting, held at the secretariat on Monday. Following the meeting, Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani briefed journalists at the conference room of the Department of Information.
Nasimul Gani said the approved holiday list includes 15 general holidays for national days and various religious festivals. Of these, 4 days will coincide with weekly holidays, comprising 2 Fridays and 2 Saturdays.
Another 14 holidays will be declared by executive order for the Bengali New Year and various religious festivals. Of these, 3 days will coincide with weekly holidays, including 1 Friday and 2 Saturdays.
As a result, 7 of the 29 holidays will overlap with weekly holidays, leaving 22 effective public holidays in 2027.
According to the approved list, employees of the Republic will be allowed up to 3 optional holidays annually for various religious festivals.
Government employees from small ethnic groups working in the Chittagong Hill Tracts and other parts of the country will also be entitled to 2 optional holidays to celebrate their main social festival, Boisabi, or similar festivals.

item.title: E-immigration launched at Shahjalal airport arrival counters, easing passenger hassle
item.description:
An automated border control system, or e-gate, has been introduced at the arrival counters of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka, allowing e-passport holders to complete immigration in just 18 to 20 seconds and avoid long queues.
The introduction of e-gates at the arrivals section has eased passenger hassle and significantly reduced the time required for immigration, officials said.
Speaking to Dhaka Tribune on Monday afternoon, Department of Immigration and Passports (DIP) Director General Major General Md Alimul Amin said e-gates had been introduced at the airport’s arrival counters and passengers could now complete immigration within a very short time.
“We also want to introduce e-gate services at departures. We are working on it,” he said.
However, he said the departure service was not yet technically ready. Although passengers’ passports can be scanned at the departure e-gates, the system cannot currently complete the required stamping process, leaving the service suspended.
During a visit to the airport, a Dhaka Tribune correspondent found that passengers still have to collect their arrival stickers manually from a police booth after completing e-immigration.
Officials said the process would be simplified once the third terminal becomes operational, and passengers would no longer have to visit the police booth separately to collect their arrival stickers.
Airport immigration officials said Bangladesh faces several technical and operational challenges in fully digitising immigration services, including e-gates and e-visa verification.
These challenges include an insufficient number of e-gates and barcode and biometric reader devices, frequent server downtime and delays in IT systems.
There is also no real-time integration among the databases of the National Identity Card (NID) system, the Department of Immigration and Passports (DIP) and the Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET).
As a result, even minor discrepancies in passengers’ names or dates of birth can prevent e-gates from automatically identifying them.
Technical problems with facial-recognition cameras and fingerprint-matching systems can also cause the gates to reject legitimate passengers. In addition, some immigration officials lack the technical expertise needed to operate digital systems and verify e-visas.
Major General Alimul Amin said several technical, institutional and practical challenges remain in converting departure immigration into a fully digital system.
“That is why the service is currently suspended. But we are working to simplify this service, as well as passport-related services, as soon as possible,” he said.
Passengers said the introduction of e-gates at arrivals had reduced both waiting time and hassle, allowing them to complete immigration automatically within 18 to 20 seconds.
Liton Kabir, who recently returned from Thailand, told Dhaka Tribune: “The e-passport was once a dream for the people of Bangladesh. The e-gate was introduced alongside it. Although the service was closed for various reasons, I feel relieved now that it has reopened. If it is introduced at departures soon, travelling will become even easier.”
Rajib Ahmed, who recently returned from Turkey, said the service had made the arrival process much easier.
“This was our first family tour. With an e-passport, you can clear immigration in about 18 seconds. It would have been great to have the facility at departures too, as it would save a lot of time. The government should pay attention to this,” he said.
An immigration official said passengers using e-gates at departures still have to return to the immigration desk for visa verification and other checks, meaning the process takes almost as long as before.
“This makes passengers angry. Data from the e-gates also often fails to reach the immigration software. That is why the departure e-gates have remained closed,” he said.
He added that while e-gates are currently closed for departing passengers at Shahjalal Airport, they are operational for arriving passengers.
Bangladesh introduced e-passports in February 2020, becoming the first country in South Asia to do so. E-gates were subsequently installed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport to facilitate faster and more efficient immigration processing.
However, technical problems and the continued need for manual visa verification and other checks created complications. As a result, passengers still had to visit immigration desks even after using the e-gates, prompting authorities to suspend their operation.
Several members of the Immigration Police's Special Branch, speaking on condition of anonymity, said around 40% of passengers using the airport each day hold e-passports.
They said the e-gates can automatically verify passport and passenger information but cannot independently verify visas.
The system also lacks provisions to automatically store information on passengers’ destinations or flights.
Consequently, visa verification continues to be conducted manually, even when passengers use the e-gates. This contributes to long queues at departure immigration, particularly when several flights arrive or depart around the same time.
Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport Executive Director Group Captain SM Ragib Samad told Dhaka Tribune that the e-gates can currently verify only passport information and cannot verify visas and other details.
“That is why the e-gates have been kept closed at departures. But we hope the service will start soon,” he said.
The government has taken an initiative to modernise Bangladesh's immigration system by integrating the existing Immigration Management System (IMS) with new technologies.
The Ministry of Home Affairs has formed a 10-member committee to review fee-setting, payment collection and settlement procedures under the system and develop an appropriate financial model.
The notice was issued on October 19 by the Departure-4 branch of the ministry's Security Services Division and published on October 25.
According to the notice, the government plans to integrate the Advance Passenger Information System (APIS), Passenger Name Record (PNR), e-Visa and Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) systems, as well as a sovereign data analytics platform, with the existing IMS.
The government is also considering appointing a third party to modernise the relevant infrastructure and implement the programme. As part of the initiative, the committee will review immigration facilitation charges, revenue collection and remittance procedures, and payment mechanisms. It will also prepare proposals on appropriate fees and a suitable financial model.
The committee is headed by the Joint Secretary of the Planning-1 wing of the Ministry of Home Affairs, while the Deputy Secretary of the Departure-4 branch will serve as its member-secretary.
Other members include the Joint Secretary of the Departure-1 wing of the Home Ministry and representatives from the Finance Division, National Board of Revenue (NBR), Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), Special Branch, Biman Bangladesh Airlines, Bangladesh Land Port Authority and the Department of Immigration and Passports.

item.title: Govt targets 3,000-4,000MW of solar power ahead of next summer
item.description:
The government aims to generate 3,000-4,000 megawatts of electricity from solar power ahead of next summer to help keep power shortages at a manageable level, State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Anindya Islam Amit said on Monday.
As part of the initiative, the government is promoting rooftop solar systems at public universities, considering them a relatively simple and effective way to expand renewable energy generation.
Speaking at a consultation meeting on installing solar power systems at 31 public universities, organized by the University Grants Commission (UGC) in Agargaon, Dhaka.
The state minister Amit said the government was working to prevent a repeat of the electricity-related hardship experienced by consumers during the current summer.
A solar power policy was formulated within two months to accelerate the expansion of solar energy, he said, adding that it could be revised based on feedback from relevant stakeholders.
The state minister emphasized that the initiative would not be imposed on universities. Decisions would instead be made based on each institution’s needs, capacity and practical circumstances, with support from the government and the UGC.
Amit said the expansion of rooftop solar power could help universities reduce carbon emissions and create opportunities to earn carbon credits.
The Power Division would support universities in obtaining carbon credits in recognition of their emissions reductions, he added.
One carbon credit generally represents the reduction or removal of one tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent. Credits may be sold after completing the required verification and certification processes.
The state minister also announced that the Bangladesh Solar Expo would be held in Dhaka on November 3-4 to promote the use of solar energy.
A separate expert meeting involving university vice-chancellors is also planned to discuss solar installations at public universities. He urged all vice-chancellors to participate.
Presiding over the meeting, UGC Chairman Professor Dr Mamun Ahmed said the consultation was organized to address confusion surrounding rooftop solar installations and gather feedback from relevant stakeholders.
The commission has already conducted a survey and formed a team to assess the feasibility of installing solar systems at its own premises and at different public universities, he said.
The UGC would provide technical assistance to universities, but no decision would be imposed on them, he added.
Mamun stressed the importance of adopting the operating expenditure (OPEX) model, under which a service provider typically finances, installs and operates a solar power system while the institution pays under an agreed contractual arrangement.
A significant portion of universities’ operating budgets goes towards electricity and gas bills, he said, adding that wider use of solar power could substantially reduce these expenses.
Referring to an initiative at Jashore University of Science and Technology (JUST), the UGC chairman said a solar power system was being pursued through a tripartite agreement under the OPEX model.
Similar arrangements could be introduced at other universities, he added.
The UGC chairman urged universities to incorporate carbon credit opportunities into their solar power plans from the outset.
He said institutions should establish mechanisms to measure the amount of carbon emissions avoided through solar power generation, which would be essential to pursuing carbon credits.
The UGC would also provide vice-chancellors with necessary guidelines, draft agreements and relevant information on installing solar systems, Mamun said.
Universities could begin implementation within a month if they took the initiative immediately, he added.
At the meeting, Professor Dr M Shamsul Alam, dean of Daffodil International University, and Tahmilur Rahman, senior assistant secretary at the Power Division, presented separate papers on rooftop solar installations at university buildings and the expansion of solar power under the OPEX model.
Among those present were Power Division Secretary Mirana Mahrook, UGC member Professor Dr Masuma Habib, JUST Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Iarul Kabir, Bangladesh University Council president and BUET Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr SM Abdur Razzak, Rajshahi University Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Md Faridul Islam, Hajee Mohammad Danesh Science and Technology University Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr M Enamullah, and UGC Secretary Dr Md Fakhrul Islam.
Other UGC members, senior officials and vice-chancellors of the 31 public universities also attended the meeting.

item.title: Cabinet clears draft law to expedite solar power installations
item.description:
The Cabinet on Monday gave approval – both in principle and final – to the draft Special Solar Power Installation Act, 2026, aimed at expediting the expansion of solar power installations across the country.
The approval came at the cabinet meeting held at the Bangladesh Secretariat with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in the chair.
The draft law was placed to turn the Special Solar Power Ordinance, 2026, already promulgated, into an act.
“The draft law was placed before the cabinet meeting for the approval. The cabinet cleared it subject to vetting by the Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division,” Cabinet Secretary Dr Nasimul Ghani said while briefing reporters after the meeting.
He said the Special Solar Power Ordinance, 2026, was promulgated under Article 93(1) of the Constitution to expedite the expansion of special solar power installation activities.
Explaining the rationale for the draft law, Nasimul Ghani said an ordinance promulgated under Article 93(1) of the Constitution must be placed before parliament at its first meeting following the promulgation, as stipulated in Article 93(2).
Following the cabinet's approval, the draft law will be placed before parliament as a bill.
Once passed by parliament and assented to by the president, it will turn into an act.
The Cabinet Secretary said the proposed law would undergo parliamentary debate, during which changes could be made if necessary.

item.title: Cabinet approves draft Public Procurement (2nd Amendment) Act, 2026
item.description:
The cabinet on Monday gave approval to the draft of the Public Procurement (Second Amendment) Act, 2026, aiming to ensure greater transparency, accountability, equal treatment and open competition in government procurement.
The approval – both in principle and final – came at the 26th cabinet meeting of the current government, chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Bangladesh Secretariat.
Cabinet Secretary Dr Nasimul Ghani briefed reporters after the meeting.
The Public Procurement Act, 2006, which serves as the principal legal framework for government procurement, has so far been amended six times.
The latest amendment was made through the Public Procurement (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, promulgated on September 21, 2026.
The ordinance was issued to introduce updated provisions aimed at protecting local industries and creating greater competition in procurement activities.
The proposed amendment includes special provisions for new, micro and small, women and disadvantaged bidders to ensure their participation in government procurement.
It also seeks to modernize the procedures under the open tendering method and expand the application of the limited tendering method to ensure a more equitable distribution of resources.
The draft law also aims to clarify provisions relating to professional misconduct and introduce alternative procurement arrangements to meet urgent state requirements.
The draft of the Public Procurement (Second Amendment) Act, 2026, was published on the websites of the Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority (BPPA) and the Implementation Monitoring and Evaluation Division (IMED) for public opinion.
An ordinance promulgated under Article 93(1) of the Constitution must be placed before Parliament at its first meeting following the promulgation, as stipulated in Article 93(2).
The cabinet gave final approval to the draft law, subject to vetting by the Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division.

item.title: Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if US agrees to demands
item.description:
Iran on Monday said it was ready to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington agrees to conditions, as US President Donald Trump issued his latest war threat at a rally for midterm elections.
A senior Iranian official said the offer to open the vital energy corridor, which follows intense efforts by mediators to stop a return to war, showed “good faith.”
Tehran has blockaded Hormuz since the war started in February, sending energy prices soaring and posing an electoral challenge for Trump. The narrow gateway to the energy-rich Gulf normally carries one-fifth of global oil consumption.
“The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran’s good-faith approach,” foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told reporters at a briefing.
“We have stated that, if Iran’s demands are met, it would be possible to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz and resume the negotiating process within a short period.”
In September, Iran proposed a seven-day plan to reopen Hormuz if the US agreed to demands including ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
Baqaei said messages were being exchanged with the United States via mediators, adding that “everything depends” on the US side accepting the Iranian demands.
“Only then can we discuss the subsequent stages.”
During final rallies for the US midterms on Tuesday, where diesel prices and consumer inflation are a key issue, Trump struck a belligerent tone, warning Iran to expect “the hammer.”
“The only reason why I’m not finished with Iran is I want to be nice. I want to try and save all those lives if I can... But at some point we’re going to have to give them the hammer,” he told voters in Iowa.
Officials from Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye have held talks with Iran in recent days, while US Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Tehran.
Oman’s ruler Sultan Haitham bin Tariq discussed the war with Chinese President Xi Jinping during a visit to Beijing on Monday, an Omani foreign ministry statement said.
“The two sides called for resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, urging the United States and Iran to pursue a peaceful path, achieve a ceasefire (and) prevent war entirely,” it said, calling for “dialogue and negotiations as soon as possible,”
China’s top diplomat also told a senior Iranian official that Beijing supports Tehran in “safeguarding its own sovereignty and security,”
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi made the remarks to Ali Bagheri Kani, deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, according to a statement from Beijing.
“All parties should... in a spirit of reason and pragmatism, focus on a political solution rather than once again resorting to armed conflict,” Wang was cited as saying.
Bagheri told Wang that “Tehran’s stance on defending its national security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity remains unchanged, and that Iran will make no compromises in this regard,” according to state TV.
In an interview with Al Jazeera released on Sunday, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Washington must accept a new route agreed between Iran and Oman for transiting the strait.
He said the US must also remove sanctions imposed in recent months and reduce American troop numbers in the region.
Washington has since August rolled out a fresh raft of sanctions, part of what it called “economic asphyxiation” of Iran.
Trump’s “hammer” comment is just the latest threat to Tehran from the US and Israel, whose joint attack marked the start of the war on February 28.
On Saturday, Trump said he still had to “take care” of one or two targets including Pickaxe mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility.
“Any act of aggression against Iran, any military attack against Iran, by whatever means, will be met with a powerful, immediate and comprehensive response from us,” Baqaei said.
At the midterms, Democrats expect to win at least partial control of Congress and impose political constraints on Trump for the first time in two years.

item.title: Iran warns new war could last longer after Trump threatens strikes
item.description:
Iran warned on Sunday that any renewed war with the United States could last longer than the previous round of fighting, after President Donald Trump said he still had to “take care” of more targets.
Diplomatic efforts to end the Middle East war have been punctuated by repeated threats from the United States and Israel to resume bombardments as they hold crucial elections.
“A potential future war could last longer than previous conflict, and the American president would not be in a position to dictate the timing or the conditions of its conclusion,” said army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia, according to Iranian state television.
In the most intense phase of the war, which began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, Tehran retaliated with missile and drone attacks across the region. Iran-aligned armed groups joined the fighting in Lebanon and Yemen.
Akraminia’s remarks followed Trump’s suggestion that the United States could swiftly strike its remaining targets in Iran.
“We still have to take care of, I would say one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes,” Trump told reporters.
“You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, and you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly,” he added, referring to a suspected underground nuclear complex.
Trump reiterated his threat on Sunday, telling a campaign rally in Iowa ahead of midterm elections, that he may have to give Tehran “the hammer” at some unspecified time.
The warning came after US media reported that Trump had held a call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday over whether and when to ramp up combat operations against the Islamic Republic.
Axios quoted one US and one Israeli official saying the two leaders discussed the state of negotiations with Iran, with Netanyahu pressing the president to strike the country immediately after Tuesday’s US midterm elections and Trump eager to let negotiations play out.
The Israeli source described the call as “tough,” while the US source said it was “direct,” according to Axios.
Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Trump confirmed he had discussed Iran with Netanyahu, but would not elaborate.
Top military and political officials in Iran have warned against any new attack.
Revolutionary Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebbi on Sunday echoed a warning issued a day earlier in a written message by Iran’s new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei.
“In a conflict with America, there are no geographical limitations; a vast theatre has been defined for inflicting damage upon the enemy,” Mohebbi said, according to state television.
Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said: “We hope the other side will exercise rationality and choose diplomacy,” adding that Iran “remains prepared for both defense and diplomacy,” according to the official IRNA news agency.
The warnings came as Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei disclosed on Saturday that he had received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance seeking to revive talks.
Rezaei noted what he described as a positive change in “tone” from the US side but said he had yet to respond.
He said Tehran had previously told Washington that unless its conditions were met, “neither would the Strait of Hormuz be reopened nor would there be any negotiations.”
Those conditions include unfreezing Iranian assets abroad, ending the months-long US naval blockade of Iranian ports, lifting longstanding sanctions and ending the war on all fronts.
Since the war began, Iran has claimed control over the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy conduit, and repeatedly targeted vessels attempting to cross without its authorization.
The United States has imposed a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports.
Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the Emirati president, said on Sunday that the United Arab Emirates hoped the exchanges would yield a breakthrough, but was preparing for the worst.
“It is not the interest of the region to go through another round... But I think we’re also, as we’ve shown before, braced for the worst,” he told a conference in Manama.
In Tehran, some residents described a sense of helplessness as threats of renewed fighting mount.
“The news coming in is truly worrying. However... there is nothing I can actually do about it,” Mohadese, a 27-year-old health inspector, told AFP.
Others including 48-year-old vendor Ebrahim saw no reason to be concerned.
“We do not fear another war; we have been at war for 48 years now -- we are always at war,” he said in downtown Tehran.

item.title: Taliban government voices ‘serious concern’ over US Afghan deportation plans
item.description:
Afghanistan’s Taliban authorities voiced concern on Monday over reported plans by Washington to deport scores of Afghan immigrants to Pakistan with the aim of their eventual return to their home country.
More than 150 Afghans in the United States would be deported via Pakistan to Afghanistan, including relatives of those who assisted US forces before their 2021 withdrawal, according to US media reports and an advocacy group.
“The Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan expresses its serious concern over reports that the United States intends to deport some Afghan refugees to Pakistan who have not yet been able to obtain legal residency documents in that country,” foreign ministry spokesman Abdul Qahar Balkhi said in a statement.
Advocacy groups have warned that the removal of former allies and their families could endanger their lives.
After regaining power, Taliban authorities announced a general amnesty for Afghans who worked with Western-backed forces and governments and have repeated promises this year that their former foes could safely return home.
However, the United Nations has recorded reports of extrajudicial killings, detentions and abuses.
President Donald Trump’s administration last year issued travel bans for a number of countries, including Afghanistan, as part of a broad immigration crackdown.
His administration sought to end deportation protections for Afghans, some of whom were granted special immigrant visas following the 2021 takeover by Taliban authorities.
Among those expected to be deported are relatives of Afghans who assisted the US military in the country prior to the fall of Kabul, according to AfghanEvac, a group seeking to help former Afghan allies.
While the United States cannot arrange deportations directly to Afghanistan, anonymous US officials told The New York Times that Pakistan will oversee their expulsion to Afghanistan.
In recent years, Germany and Turkey have deported Afghan nationals directly to Afghanistan, despite concerns from human rights groups over the risks facing returnees.
Balkhi said Taliban authorities urged “the United States of America to adopt a responsible and measured approach in this regard and to take any decisions and measures regarding the fate of Afghan citizens with clear mutual understanding, necessary coordination, and consideration of the rights and legitimate demands of the individuals concerned.”
“The Afghan side is ready to interact in this regard in a practical and mutually understanding manner,” he added.
Pakistan’s government earlier this year ordered law enforcement nationwide to arrest Afghan citizens without visas as part of a years-long repatriation policy that has pushed back millions of Afghans who fled throughout decades of war.
Relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan have been fraught since the Taliban authorities took power and worsened after deadly border clashes last October that led to near-total closure of the border.

item.title: Democrats, Trump hold final rallies before midterm elections
item.description:
Democrats teed up final get-out-the-vote rallies Monday on the eve of midterm elections where they expect to win at least partial control of Congress and impose political constraints on President Donald Trump for the first time in two years.
Rallies -- including by star Democratic Senate candidates James Talarico in Texas and Adam Hamilton in Kansas -- were capping a campaign of breathtaking tension and bitterness.
For his closing argument, Trump chose a speech in Washington at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool -- a landmark that has become synonymous with the 80-year-old president’s obsessive, controversial drive to redevelop the US capital.
“We’re going to win,” he said on Sunday.
Polls, however, show that Democrats are near certain to take the majority from Republicans in the House of Representatives and have a real shot at winning the currently Republican Senate.
Even winning just the House would mean Democrats have voting power over the federal budget and would lead powerful committees able to investigate alleged corruption under Trump, the Epstein files and other explosive issues.
The loss of total Republican dominance would push Trump into unfamiliar and uncomfortable territory: a lame-duck period beset with high inflation at home, the sputtering war against Iran and hostile Democratic investigations into his activities in Washington.
But a decade into the Trump era, Democrats remain wary about predictions of victory.
“Nauseously optimistic,” Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock told CNN to describe the mood.
Democrats are facing late internal divisions, with left-wing candidates clashing at times with the party’s establishment.
In a startling display of infighting on Sunday, Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens in Michigan endorsed Republican candidate Mike Rogers against left-wing progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed in her state’s key Senate race.
Trump was quick to praise Stevens for her “bravery,” posting on his Truth Social platform that “Haley said what few people are willing to say.”
Stevens, who lost a bruising primary to El-Sayed in August despite being backed by the Democratic establishment, struggled to explain her decision in an interview with CNN.
“It’s just where I was at the end of the night and earlier this morning,” she said.
Trump’s Republicans have fought a political scorched-earth campaign, painting Democrats as communists and openly branding El-Sayed, who is Muslim, as a terrorist.
Addressing a crowd in Iowa on Sunday, Trump said Democrats are “extreme and dangerous radicals” who will “steal your wealth” and let in migrants to “ransack, rape and plunder.”
But polls show Americans heavily souring on Trump’s wrecking-ball act.
An NBC News poll released on Sunday showed 60 percent disapprove of his performance, particularly over high prices exacerbated by his now eight-month-long war against Iran.
While the House seems highly likely to turn Democratic, the battle for the Senate is up in the air.
Only a third of the Senate’s 100 seats are being contested in these midterms, and few of the races were seen as favorable to Democrats.
However, with surprisingly strong challenges in deeply Republican states, pollsters now say the odds of a Democratic flip are at minimum even.
The final New York Times/Siena poll released Sunday evening showed Democratic candidates leading in all seven seats viewed as most competitive, though five remained within the margin of error.
A Democratic Senate would be able to shut down Trump’s lifetime appointments to courts -- including the Supreme Court.
While Tuesday is election day, early voting has already seen a record 54 million people cast ballots around the country.
The midterms have seen about $11 billion spent on advertising, with large chunks coming from individual mega-donors.
Elon Musk, a close Trump ally who led the so-called DOGE effort in dismantling entire government departments, has given a staggering nearly half-billion dollars to help get Republicans elected.

item.title: Faruk Ahmed appointed new SRB DG
item.description:
Faruk Ahmed, additional inspector general (additional IGP) of Bangladesh Highway Police, has been appointed as the new director general (DG) of the Special Response Battalion (SRB).
The Ministry of Home Affairs issued a notification in this regard on Tuesday.
Meanwhile, Md Ahsan Habib Palash, director general of the Special Response Battalion, has been transferred to the Police Headquarters in Dhaka.
A 17th BCS (Police) officer, Faruk joined the Bangladesh Police as an Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) in 1998.
The Special Response Battalion formally begun its operations on September 16 as a specialised unit of Bangladesh Police following the publication of the Special Response Battalion (SRB) Act, 2026 in the gazette.
Besides, Additional Inspector General of Police Md Sayedur Rahman of Police Headquarters has been transferred to the Highway Police.
Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Md Ashique Sayed has been appointed as the commissioner of Gazipur Metropolitan Police (GMP).
Meanwhile, incumbent GMP Commissioner Md Israil Hawlader has been promoted to Additional IGP and posted to the Industrial Police. Additional IGP Gazi Jasim Uddin of the Industrial Police has been transferred to the Police Telecom Organisation, Dhaka.
DIG Mir Ashraf Ali, who was serving in the Railway Police, has been posted to the Rajshahi Range, replacing Ashique Sayed, who was serving as its DIG.
All the transfers and postings would take effect immediately, said the notification.

DU leads Bangladesh in QS Asia rankings
item.description:
The University of Dhaka (DU) has retained its position as Bangladesh’s top-ranked university in the QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027, although it slipped four places to 136th in the regional rankings compared with last year.
The rankings were released on Tuesday by international higher education ranking agency Quacquarelli Symonds (QS), featuring more than 1,720 universities across 26 higher education systems.
North South University (NSU) ranked second among Bangladeshi universities, retaining its 149th position in Asia. Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET) placed third nationally, dropping 14 places to 179th.
A total of 52 Bangladeshi universities featured in this year’s rankings, taking the country’s representation above 50 for the first time. In 2017, only two Bangladeshi universities were included.
According to QS, 12 Bangladeshi universities improved their positions, seven retained their previous rankings and 27 slipped. Six institutions made their debut. However, the number of Bangladeshi universities among Asia’s top 500 fell from 16 last year to 14.
Daffodil International University advanced five places to 216th, while BRAC University dropped 11 places to 271st. Jahangirnagar University fell 25 places to 329th, and Rajshahi University slipped 37 places to 349th.
Khulna University of Engineering and Technology (KUET) made a significant improvement, climbing 44 places to 370th. Bangladesh Agricultural University retained its 378th position.
Gazipur Agricultural University, formerly Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Agricultural University, entered Asia’s top 500 for the first time, ranking 407th.
The QS report said Bangladeshi universities performed relatively well in the citations per paper indicator. Three local universities ranked among Asia’s top 10 in this category, while 10 made it into the top 100. Bangladesh ranked fifth in Asia based on the average score in this indicator.
However, the report highlighted weaknesses in faculty-student ratios, the proportion of academic staff holding PhDs, international faculty and student exchange programmes. No Bangladeshi university made Asia’s top 200 in any of these indicators.
Among Asian universities, the University of Hong Kong topped the rankings, followed by Peking University of China. Tsinghua University, also in China, climbed six places to third.

item.title: World Bank: Bangladesh has two more decades to harness demographic dividend
item.description:
Bangladesh has roughly two decades before its working-age population share peaks in 2045, offering a crucial but temporary window to turn rapid demographic shifts into economic opportunity, according to a new World Bank report Tuesday.
While Bangladesh has more time than most of its regional peers, structural obstacles urgently require action, warns the report, titled Demographic Change in South Asia: From Tailwinds to Headwinds for Development .
Across South Asia, the working-age population numbering 1.17 billion people will peak and begin shrinking in less than 10 years.
By 2049, South Asia is projected to become an aged regional economy, with 14 percent of its population aged 65 and older. Bangladesh is expected to hit aged status in 2051.
Since 2000, an expanding share of prime-age adult workers has added 0.4% annually to South Asia's GDP and boosted labor productivity by 1.1% per year.
However, the region's demographic transition from an aging to an aged population is moving faster—and at lower per capita income levels—than in comparable emerging and developing economies.
As a result, the annual contribution of demographics to GDP growth is projected to shrink to just 0.1% between now and 2050.
“South Asian economies are aging faster and earlier in their development journeys,” said Johannes Zutt, World Bank vice president for South Asia.
“They need to act now to adopt policies and build infrastructure that create more and better jobs and deepen the gains from their ‘youth dividend’, while at the same time preparing for aging. This will enable South Asia to make the most of its large working age population and lay the foundations for a ‘second dividend’ as healthier older people continue contributing to the economy.”
The report highlights a persistent jobs gap in Bangladesh, where a favorable age structure has not fully translated into higher employment or productivity gains.
This shortfall is driven by limited formal job creation, low female labor-force participation, and lingering human capital gaps.
Approximately 84% of Bangladeshi workers—around 58 million people—are informally employed.
Higher education offers little guarantee of formal work, with 44% of university graduates holding informal jobs.
Furthermore, formal firms are expanding employment slowly, while small enterprises have, on average, shed workers recently.
“Bangladesh’s demographic opportunity depends on what it does now: help firms create better jobs, equip young people with market-relevant skills, and remove barriers that keep women out of work,” said Jean Pesme, World Bank division director for Bangladesh and Bhutan.
“At the same time, the country needs to start strengthening healthcare and old age income security for an aging population. That means meeting the growing financing need for aging transition will require stronger domestic resource mobilization.”
Systems for healthcare, long-term care, and pensions across South Asia remain poorly equipped for a population living longer without necessarily living healthier.
Currently, only 17% of the region's working-age population contributes to a pension scheme, and just 10% of older South Asians receive pension benefits—the lowest coverage rate worldwide.
To navigate this transition, the report recommends a dual strategy: sustaining the primary "youth dividend" by boosting job productivity, expanding MSME access to finance, streamlining regulations, enhancing education and health systems, and promoting female employment; and unlocking a "second dividend" through expanded healthcare, long-term care, pension safety nets, and increased national savings to raise long-term productivity.

item.title: Private sector credit growth dips further in September
item.description:
Private sector credit growth fell to a historic low of 4.17% in September 2026 amid a prolonged slowdown in economic activity.
Growth has remained below 5% for seven consecutive months, as demand for loans has weakened mainly due to inadequate energy supplies and geopolitical tensions, according to bankers.
They also said most banks had become cautious about approving fresh loans to avoid repayment risks amid a rise in non-performing loans (NPLs) across the banking sector.
The private sector credit growth came down to 4.17% in September 2026 on a year-on-year basis from 4.75% a month ago, according to Bangladesh Bank's provisional data.
It was 2.63-percentage points lower than the Bangladesh Bank (BB) target of 6.80% for the first half (H1) of current FY27.
The private sector credit growth stood at 4.72% in March, 4.75% in April, 4.98% in May, 4.47% in June, 4.62% in July, and 4.75% in August, the central bank data showed.
The central bank had announced the stimulus package aimed at reviving economic activities and supporting businesses affected by the prolonged slowdown.
Besides, the banking regulator has already taken several measures to encourage banks to resume lending, including facilities for loan rescheduling and restructuring.
Classified loans in the country's banking sector ballooned to Tk606,000 crore as of June 2026, accounting for 32.78% of the entire loans worth Tk1,850,000 crore disbursed by all scheduled banks.

item.title: Global food, fuel price hike poses concerns for Bangladesh
item.description:
Global food and energy prices are set to rise sharply this year and stay under pressure in 2027, which could add to inflationary pressures in import-dependent economies such as Bangladesh.
The World Bank’s Commodity Markets Outlook, released on October 28, projects global commodity prices to rise 23% in 2026.
The main drivers are a 32% jump in energy prices amid the Middle East conflict, disrupted grain shipments, and weather risks linked to a strong El Niño.
Food commodity prices are expected to rise about 10% in 2026 and a further 7% in 2027, a cumulative increase of about 18%.
The bank warned that the combined shocks could worsen inflation and food insecurity in vulnerable economies.
The report does not give a Bangladesh-specific forecast for food inflation or domestic prices.
Bangladesh’s exposure will depend on international prices, import costs, exchange rates, and how much is passed on to consumers.
Year-on-year food inflation in South Asia rose to 5.8% in the third quarter of 2026, above the region’s 2010–19 average of 5.6%.
The bank said projected increases in grain and vegetable oil prices are likely to intensify these pressures.
Rice prices were 24% higher than a year earlier in the third quarter of the year, from July to September 2026, amid El Niño-related weather concerns in South and Southeast Asia.
The bank forecasts rice to rise 10% in 2026 and 12% in 2027, as global production is expected to fall for the first time in a decade.
Wheat prices are projected to jump 28% in 2026 and 14% in 2027.
In the third quarter of the year, grain prices rose 9% and stood 25% higher than a year earlier, while wheat rose 13% and was 40% higher.
The bank’s overall food price index remained 12% above its year-earlier level in October.
Energy prices are projected to rise 32% in 2026, reversing three years of declines.
Brent crude is forecast to average $91 a barrel this year, against $69 in 2025, before easing to $79 in 2027.
Global oil supply is projected to fall 5.2% in 2026, the largest drop in more than four decades outside 2020.
Asian LNG prices were almost three times their pre-conflict levels in mid-October, as Gulf supply remained constrained.
Fertilizer prices are expected to rise 14% in 2026 after an early-year surge in urea, then fall 12% in 2027.
Higher fuel and fertilizer costs can raise farming and transport expenses, which is why these movements matter for a country that relies on imported energy and agricultural inputs.
Metal prices are set to reach a new high in 2026, rising 25% as prices of aluminum, copper, and tin all hit record highs.
These gains reflect strong demand from investments in renewable energy, electric vehicles, and data centers, together with supply disruptions this year.
Prices are expected to decline by 3% in 2027.
Precious metals prices are forecast to increase by 40% in 2026 as demand for safe-haven assets remains elevated amid geopolitical and policy uncertainty.
They are expected to moderate somewhat in 2027 but remain more than three times their 2015–19 average.
The report names Bangladesh in its discussion of tea. It says El Niño could reduce tea production and quality in South Asia, particularly in Bangladesh and parts of India.
All South Asian countries are highly or moderately exposed to El Niño, according to the report.
The market picture is more balanced.
The global tea market remains well supplied, helped by rising production in northern India and Bangladesh.
The report does not forecast a specific decline in Bangladesh’s output.
Tea prices at the Colombo and Kolkata auctions fell 1% in the third quarter as weak demand outweighed weather-related output losses.
The bank expects tea prices to rise 4% in 2027 and 2% in 2028 as demand recovers, particularly in the Middle East.
Overall commodity prices are forecast to fall 7% in 2027, but the outlook is vulnerable to geopolitical and weather shocks.
If higher energy prices, attacks on Black Sea grain shipments, and a very strong El Niño combine, Brent could average $105 in 2027.
Food prices could be 12% above the baseline, and grain prices could be 20% higher, exceeding 2022 levels for food.
The bank said such a scenario could push more people into extreme poverty.
The World Bank Group has made $50–60 billion available through existing instruments, including $25 billion in pre-arranged financing, to support safety nets for vulnerable people, fiscal capacity, and working capital for firms and farms.
“Commodity markets are being hit by several major shocks at once,” said Ayhan Kose, World Bank’s deputy chief economist and director of the Prospects Group.
“Higher energy costs and trade disruptions are driving up prices across a broad range of commodities, threatening to worsen inflation, food insecurity, and economic growth. The priority must be to protect the poorest people and support low-income countries already struggling with heavy debt burdens.” Ayhan added.

item.title: Minister: Rooppur plant may supply power to national grid before December
item.description:
The Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant may begin supplying electricity to the national grid before December if everything goes according to plan, Science and Technology Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam has said.
He made the remarks on Tuesday in response to a question from journalists at a press conference at the Secretariat ahead of the Bangladesh AI Business Summit 2026.
The minister said the plant was currently at the C-stage of commissioning, with each phase requiring clearance from the relevant regulatory authorities before proceeding to the next.
The plant has so far reached 20% thermal capacity. Once it reaches 35-40%, the steam generated will be used to turn the turbine, which will drive the generator to produce electricity, he said.
However, several tests remain before the plant can begin generating electricity, the minister said, stressing that safety would not be compromised under any circumstances.
He said equipment would be dismantled, tested and repaired if necessary until satisfactory results were achieved. The process could be repeated two, three or even four times to ensure safety. The plant would not supply electricity to the national grid until all safety requirements were fully met.
Fakir Mahbub Anam said the plant could start supplying electricity within the next five to six weeks, provided progress remains on track. However, he declined to set a firm deadline, citing the extensive technical tests and safety procedures involved in commissioning a nuclear power plant.
He also said it had taken nearly two months to resolve an issue involving a VVR valve, which was eventually addressed in coordination with Russian contractor Rosatom.
Outlining the production plan, the minister said the plant would initially generate 300MW, with output gradually increased in phases.
The authorities expect generation to exceed 1,100MW within the first six months, although the pace of expansion will depend on progress made by scientists and technical experts working at the site.

item.title: PM orders advancing plans for 2nd Padma, Jamuna bridges and Padma Barrage
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Tuesday directed officials to advance plans for a second Padma Bridge, a second Jamuna Bridge and the Padma Barrage, prioritising improved connectivity in the southwestern and northern regions.
He gave the directives at a meeting with officials of the relevant ministries and divisions at the Prime Minister’s Office in the Bangladesh Secretariat in the afternoon, said PM’s Assistant Press Secretary Abdullah Al Mahmud Shahriar.
The meeting was informed that feasibility studies for the second Padma and Jamuna bridges are underway.
Final decisions on their locations, designs and estimated costs will be made after the studies are completed in September next year.
The proposed second Padma Bridge was discussed with a focus on a Y-shaped connection system, while improved connectivity for Rangpur and other northern districts was highlighted in planning the second Jamuna Bridge.
The second Padma Bridge, if built, will improve communication between the capital and the southwestern region.
It will also provide alternative connectivity to Mongla seaport and the Benapole and Darshana land ports.
The meeting also discussed the Padma Barrage project, including its potential to address dry-season water shortages, boost agricultural production, maintain river flows and environmental balance, and create road connectivity across the barrage.
Issues relating to project financing, land acquisition, rehabilitation and coordination among the relevant ministries and agencies also came up for discussion.
Road Transport and Bridges, Railways and Shipping Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam, State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Mir Shahe Alam, State Minister for Railways and Road Transport and Highways Habibur Rashid, State Minister for Water Resources Farhad Hossain Azad and State Minister for Shipping and Bridges Division Md Razib Ahsan attended the meeting.
Finance Secretary Dr Md Khairuzzaman Majumder, Bridges Division Secretary Mohammad Abdur Rauf, Water Resources Secretary Dr AKM Shahabuddin, Road Transport and Highways Division Secretary Dr Mohammad Ziaul Haque and other senior officials were also present.

item.title: Bangladesh Bank relaxes rules to allow Tk 30b loan to City Group
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank has suspended a provision of the Bank Company Act to facilitate a Tk 30 billion working capital loan to five defaulting companies of City Group, one of the country's leading industrial conglomerates.

According to a Bangladesh Bank notification, the five loan-defaulting companies of City Group are City Seed Crushing Industries Ltd, City Sugar Industries Ltd, City Edible Oil Ltd, City Dal Mills Ltd and Shampa Flour Mills Ltd.

The relevant provision of the Bank Company Act will not apply to the syndicated financing, led by City Bank, to provide working capital facilities worth Tk 30 billion to these companies.

Bangladesh Bank issued a notification today granting the exemption.

Section 27KaKa(3) of the Bank Company Act has been suspended for City Group until December next year. Under this provision, a loan-defaulting company is not eligible to obtain fresh loans.

Bangladesh Bank Deputy Governor Kabir Ahmed issued the notification suspending the provision until December next year. As a result, City Group, which markets products under the Teer brand, will face no further regulatory hurdles in obtaining fresh loans.

At a meeting held at Bangladesh Bank on 25 October, the central bank advised the lending banks not to classify City Group's loans as defaulted at this stage. It also suggested that the conglomerate be given facilities for long-term loan restructuring and rescheduling, if necessary, to help it overcome its difficulties and resume normal operations.

In addition, an initiative was taken to form a consortium of the lending banks to provide the conglomerate with the working capital needed to continue its business.

The group owes more than Tk 260 billion to 43 banks, and these loans have already become classified as defaulted. Bangladesh Bank Governor Mostakur Rahman, top executives of several lending banks and City Group Managing Director Md Hasan attended the tripartite meeting at the central bank.

The notification issued today also sets out several conditions.

It states that neither the government nor Bangladesh Bank will incur any liability arising from the proposed loan facility. In the future, City Bank or any other bank or financial institution participating in the consortium will not be entitled to seek any form of financial assistance from the government or Bangladesh Bank.

To ensure adequate collateral against the proposed loan facility, City Group will provide registered mortgages on properties that are not already encumbered by any of its other loans or liabilities.

The proceeds from selling goods purchased with the syndicated loan must be deposited into a designated bank account. Payments to the participating banks against the syndicated loan facility must then be made regularly from that account on a proportionate basis, with priority given to settling their dues.

The notification further states that the raw materials imported using the syndicated loan will be purchased by the lending banks of the borrowing companies, acting through a security agent, and processed under their custody.

item.title: HSC: Students who fail in up to 2 subjects can retake exams on 1 Dec
item.description:
Students who failed in up to two subjects in this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations will have the opportunity to retake only the subjects they failed.

The supplementary examinations will begin on 1 December. Both regular and irregular candidates will be eligible to sit for these examinations.

The Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee announced this in a notice. It said the examination schedule would be published later on the respective education boards' websites.

HSC results 2026 re-scrutiny applications open from Sunday

Currently, under the existing system for public examinations such as the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) and HSC, candidates who fail in one or more subjects have to wait a year to retake the examinations.

They can choose to sit for only the subjects they failed or retake all subjects.

As a result, students who fail in just one or two subjects have to wait an entire year for another opportunity.

HSC results re-scrutiny: Applications open, here’s how to apply

This time, the education authorities have decided to arrange retake examinations within a month for candidates who failed in no more than two subjects.

The HSC and equivalent examinations concluded on 31 October.

A total of 422,905 candidates failed in one or two subjects this year. Of them, 298,040 failed in one subject, while 124,865 failed in two subjects.

LDC graduation is deferred by three years. Does it make things better?
item.description:
Last December, I argued in this column that Bangladesh should graduate from least developed country status on schedule in 2026. I argued against deferral for three reasons.
First , it sends a wrong signal to the investors, that even though we passed all the markers for graduation we are not ready to accept it, which means our fundamentals remained weak and the economy was weaker than we had been projecting.
Second , the delay would fix nothing. We would be buying time but time does not fix our woes.
Third , I asked that the debate shifts from when or whether to graduate to preparing for graduation so that we benefit from it.
For me, LDC graduation is a stress test. But the deferral has happened and we now have three years. Does it make things better or worse?
The resolution grants the extension on an exceptional basis, and the graduation framework does not treat a domestic political transition as grounds for one. This was a concession and it is not a precedent.
Attached to it is an obligation to implement a national smooth transition strategy and report progress to the Committee for Development Policy every year. The Committee has also revised its supplementary indicators for the 2027 review to a set of 44, calling the change a shift from once-off measurement to continuous assessment.
We will be judged every year, in public, on a trajectory rather than a snapshot, and no stated ground is left on which to ask for more time.
What is the case for the deferral?
Merchandise exports were $48 billion in FY2025-26, of which readymade garments accounted for $38.70bn, about four-fifths of our export.
The European Union took $19.06bn of those garment exports. Nearly three-quarters of everything we sell abroad moves under duty-free terms we hold only because we are a least developed country, and that share has to find new terms by 2029.
Two things change when that access ends; the tariff is the smaller of them. The first is the rule of origin.
Everything But Arms lets imported fabric made up into garments here qualify as ours, while standard preferences require both the fabric and the garment to be made in Bangladesh.
We import about 60% of our woven fabric, so a large part of the woven trade would fail that test and bear the full tariff whichever scheme we sit under.
The second change is the duty itself, as European Union tariffs on apparel run at about 11.8% at the most-favoured-nation rate and 9.6% under standard preferences, against zero today.
The published estimates of what this costs differ by a factor of three. UNCTAD's Trade Preferences Outlook 2025 puts the annual loss above $17.5bn, a fall of 32%, with 77% of it in the European Union alone.
SANEM puts it near 11% of exports and the UN readiness assessment at between 5.5% and 15%, where UNCTAD's own earlier modelling also sat.
The spread is not a dispute about arithmetic. It turns on whether our garments pay the full tariff or fall back on standard preferences.
Against last year's $48bn, the bill is somewhere between $2.6bn and more than $17bn a year, and we are preparing without knowing which.
Our external position is already resting on remittances rather than on exports. The trade deficit reached $27.28bn in FY2025-26 and the current account closed about $1.6bn in deficit. Record remittances of $35.6bn held reserves at $36.21bn in mid-October. An export loss at the modest end of those estimates lands on that arithmetic, as no second earner can absorb it.
The timing is worse than the amount. External debt stood at $78.22bn in March and 62% of it is concessional. Debt service rises from $4.11bn in FY25 to a projected $7.6bn by FY29, the year the preferences end, and graduation closes the windows that made the debt cheap.
The debt is already about 140% of annual exports, and that ratio worsens from both directions if exports fall while servicing rises at market rates.
Last December, the IMF put our growth near 3.5% with inflation easing. In October, it cut the projection for this year to 3.2%, the weakest since 1988-89, and raised inflation to 10.9%.
The World Bank expects the weakness to persist through FY28, two of the three years we have been given, and private sector credit growth fell to 4.5% in June, a 33-year low.
A diversified export base is built out of investment in laboratories, certification, cold chain, and reliable power, and none of that is financed out of 3.2% growth.
First , the choice is not ours. Graduation follows from meeting the thresholds at two consecutive reviews, and at the 2024 review our income per head stood at $2,684 against a threshold of $1,306, the Human Assets Index at 77.5 against 66, and the vulnerability index at 21.9 where 32 or below qualifies. A government can ask for time, which we have now done, and after that the question is closed.
Second , the preferences are worth less every year even if we keep them, as a margin of preference is only the gap between our duty and our competitors'. Vietnam already sells into the European Union under a trade agreement and India is negotiating one, so that gap narrows on its own.
Third, the preferences shape what we make. They apply to the goods we already produce, so they reward more of the same, and a quarter-century of duty-free access to Europe has left one sector supplying four-fifths of exports. A country off the list negotiates agreements instead of receiving concessions, and an agreement can be written for a product we do not yet sell. The loss above is the price of the transition rather than a permanent cut in what we can earn.
First , the Ministry of Commerce should obtain a written position from the European Commission, before the 2027 review, on whether our apparel qualifies for GSP+ or standard preferences. On Mohiuddin Rubel's reading of the safeguard threshold, it qualifies for neither, and every other decision depends on the answer.
Second , the government should ratify the outstanding conventions required for GSP+ and file the first implementation reports by December 2027, as the scheme rests on a record of enforcement.
Third , the Ministry of Textiles should publish an annual target for domestically produced woven fabric, beginning this fiscal year, as the origin rule applies to the fabric rather than to the duty.
Fourth , it should bring the agreements with Japan and South Korea into force by December 2027 and conclude one more by the end of 2028.
Fifth , the national accreditation board should secure European recognition of its certificates by 2028, as a buyer who will not accept our test report needs no tariff to refuse our goods.
Sixth , the Directorate General of Drug Administration should settle licensing before November 2029 for the fifth to a quarter of locally made medicines patented abroad, as a 4% royalty adds 2% to 3% to the price of a generic.
Seventh , the Ministry of Finance should release the annual progress report at home when it submits it to the Committee, stating the target, the deadline and the responsible ministry for each item above.
Every one of the seven can be completed before November 2029, provided each has a named ministry and a date set against it in writing. Otherwise the three years will pass as the past year has.
Md Rubaiyath Sarwar is Managing Director of Innovision Consulting, a Trustee of Panam Institute.

item.title: CPC International Department chief arrives in Dhaka on three-day visit
item.description:
Minister of the International Department of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee Liu Haixing arrived in Dhaka on Tuesday night on a three-day visit to Bangladesh.
During his visit, Liu is scheduled to meet President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. He will also attend a political dialogue, programs on Bangladesh-China relations and other engagements.
He arrived at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at 11pm on Tuesday aboard an Emirates Airlines flight, said Prime Minister's Deputy Press Secretary Jahidul Islam Rony.
BNP Standing Committee Member and Prime Minister's Public Administration Affairs Adviser Ismail Zabiullah, BNP Vice Chairman Air Vice Marshal (Retd) Altaf Hossain Chowdhury and BNP Joint Secretaries General Khairul Kabir Khokon, Syed Emran Saleh Prince, Advocate Abdus Salam Azad and Prime Minister's Protocol Officer Kamrul Islam, among others, welcomed the Chinese delegation at the airport.
Liu will begin his engagements on Wednesday at 8:20am by paying homage at the mausoleums of Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman and former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar in the capital.
He is scheduled to pay a courtesy call on Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Bangladesh Secretariat at 10:00 am on the same day.
The Chinese delegation accompanying Liu during the meeting will include Chinese Embassy Charge d'Affaires in Dhaka Dr Liu Yuyin, Director General of the CPC International Department's Bureau of Southeast and South Asian Affairs Peng Xiubin, Director General of its Public
Information and Communication Bureau Hu Zhaoming, Deputy Director General-level official of the Bureau of Southeast and South Asian Affairs Li Jinyan, Director of the same bureau Wang Siqi, and Deputy Division Director of the department's General Office and Minister's Assistant Liu Chengxiao.
The delegation also includes English interpreter Shi Meiqi and department officials Chen Yongpei, Zhang Guyu, Liu Hongru and He Yiyang.
Following the meeting with the Prime Minister, Liu will pay a courtesy call on the President at Bangabhaban at 11am. He will also visit Bangabhaban and attend a welcome luncheon hosted by the President.
From 2pm to 3:30pm, the Chinese delegation leader will attend a roundtable discussion titled 'Where History Illuminates the Future: China-Bangladesh Political Parties Plus' at the Crystal Ballroom of Hotel InterContinental in Dhaka.
He is also scheduled to attend the inauguration of the Bangladesh-China Centre for Party and State Governance Studies at the event.
Liu will visit the Bangladesh National Museum from 3:45pm before visiting the site of the former Chinese Embassy chancery building and the current chancery in Dhaka.
In the evening, he will attend a dinner hosted by Prime Minister's Political Adviser and BNP Acting Secretary General Advocate Ruhul Kabir Rizvi at Pan Pacific Sonargaon Hotel at 7pm.
On the final day of his visit on Thursday, Liu will attend a livelihood support distribution programme at Shamsul Haque Khan School and College at 8:45am.
He will then join a breakfast meeting with Foreign Affairs State Minister Humaiun Kobir at the State Guest House Padma.
The Chinese delegation leader is scheduled to leave Dhaka at 12:50 pm on Thursday.

item.title: Journalists’ views to get priority in finalizing Cyber Security Act draft
item.description:
A meeting at the Posts and Telecommunications Division in Dhaka on Wednesday emphasized giving priority to the views of journalists and media representatives in finalizing the draft Cyber Security (Amendment) Act 2026.
The meeting also placed particular weight on ensuring that the law is not used in any way as a tool to harass journalists, the media or independent journalism.
The meeting of the cabinet committee formed to review and finalize the draft of the Cyber Security (Amendment) Act 2026 was held on Wednesday at the meeting room of the Posts and Telecommunications Division with Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam in the chair, according to a ministry press release.
The meeting held detailed discussions on the opinions of various stakeholders, recommendations of journalists and observations of the ministries and agencies concerned.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed and State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam were present.
For the protection of journalists and the media, the meeting discussed and reached an in-principle consensus on keeping a provision requiring prior permission from the court having jurisdiction before arresting any journalist, media owner or responsible person over news published or broadcast in the media, said the release.
It added that emphasis was also laid on following due legal process and preventing harassment in taking action against journalists.
The meeting also discussed a proposal to consider defamation, disparagement and cyberbullying separately and to rearrange the relevant sections of the law. It also discussed making the definition of cyberspace more specific.
Importance was also given to maintaining consistency with the Penal Code in the definition of and punishment for defamation. Opinions were also given on making the definitions of rumor and disinformation clearer and more specific so that press freedom is not undermined by vague or overly broad definitions in the law.
The meeting also discussed not including a provision for mobile courts in the law, informing the person or organization concerned of the reasons when content is removed or blocked, and fixing a timeframe for disposing of applications to unblock blocked content.
A proposal to issue a written notice and give an opportunity for self-defense before taking action against any media outlet or organization was also discussed.
The meeting also discussed the composition of the Cyber Security Council, media representation and consultation with international stakeholders.
Emphasis was laid on the concerned ministry holding discussions in coordination with development partners, including the United Nations, and international technology platforms such as Meta.
The meeting discussed refining the amended draft law further on the basis of stakeholders' opinions and recommendations and publishing it on the website. Emphasis was laid on making the draft more acceptable, effective and timely by taking public opinion.
Speakers at the meeting said the Cyber Security law must be framed by maintaining a balance between preventing cybercrime and protecting citizens' rights, freedom of expression and press freedom.
They said efforts to finalize the draft, taking into account the constructive opinions of all stakeholders concerned, will continue.
A presentation was made at the meeting on behalf of the National Cyber Security Agency.
Senior officials of the ministries and divisions concerned were present at the meeting.

item.title: Government plans to procure 5,830 vehicles for police
item.description:
A long-standing shortage of transport in the police force is set to be addressed through a major government initiative to procure 5,830 vehicles at a cost of Tk6,608 crore, aimed at improving mobility and strengthening field operations.
The proposed fleet includes pickup vans, jeeps, buses, ambulances, prison vans, speedboats, riot-control vehicles, armoured vehicles and specialised vehicles suitable for operations in remote and difficult-to-access areas.
The vehicles will be procured under two separate projects. Of the total allocation, Tk4,328 crore has been proposed for the purchase of 4,829 operational vehicles, while Tk2,280.14 crore will be spent on 1,001 specialized vehicles. The projects also include provisions for training police personnel in vehicle operation, repair and maintenance.
The main objective is to strengthen the police force's capacity to combat crime, conduct regular patrols, respond quickly to emergencies and maintain public order.
The two projects were placed for approval at the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (Ecnec) meeting on Wednesday. Following approval, the projects are scheduled to be implemented between October 2026 and June 2029.
According to the home ministry, police provide services across nearly 147,000 square kilometres of the country through 639 administrative police stations. However, the force currently has only 1,237 vehicles to serve these areas, meaning that each police station has fewer than two vehicles on average. Around 64% of the existing vehicles are more than 10 years old.
In addition, 455 police vehicles were burnt across the country during the 2024 student-people uprising, while another 1,074 vehicles were damaged. This further aggravated the shortage.
The ageing vehicles frequently break down during operations, making regular patrols, crime prevention and rapid responses to emergencies increasingly difficult.
Home ministry officials said many police stations have to manage law and order across their entire jurisdictions with just one pickup van. Ensuring an adequate supply of vehicles has therefore become essential. The addition of new vehicles is expected to improve police mobility at the field level and enable the rapid deployment of personnel and equipment when needed.
Asked about the initiative, Mirza Mohammad Ali Reza, joint secretary of the Planning-1 Wing of the Home Ministry of Home Affairs, said two projects had been sent to the Planning Commission to strengthen police capacity.
"A total of 5,830 vehicles will be procured to enhance the operational capacity of the police," he said.
"Many police stations have only one pickup van. How can they maintain law and order with that? How can the police perform their duties without the necessary logistical support?" he added.
Under the project titled “Procurement of Operational Vehicles for Capacity Enhancement of Bangladesh Police,” the government has proposed purchasing 4,829 vehicles at an estimated cost of Tk4,328 crore.
Double-cabin pickup vans account for the largest share of the proposed procurement. A total of 2,909 pickups will be purchased at an estimated cost of Tk2,501.74 crore, with each vehicle priced at Tk86 lakh.
The project also includes 400 jeeps with 2,700cc engines for senior police officials at a cost of Tk676 crore. Another 345 jeeps with 2,000cc engines will be procured at an estimated cost of Tk258.75 crore.
In addition, the government plans to purchase 214 microbuses at Tk52 lakh each, 148 non-air-conditioned large buses at the same unit price and 148 air-conditioned minibuses at Tk1.20 crore each. These vehicles will be used for the transportation of police personnel and to support the activities of different units.
The list of operational vehicles also includes 115 prison vans, 100 patrol cars and 50 ambulances.
To strengthen police operations along river routes, the project proposes procuring 100 speedboats at a cost of Tk80 crore.
The second project aims to strengthen the police force's capacity to handle special situations, maintain public order, investigate crimes and conduct operations in remote areas, alongside its regular activities.
Under the project titled “Procurement of Specialised Vehicles for Capacity Enhancement of Bangladesh Police,” 1,001 specialised vehicles will be purchased at an estimated cost of Tk2,280.14 crore.
To deal with situations such as labour unrest in industrial areas, the project proposes purchasing 11 armoured personnel carriers (APCs) at a cost of Tk132 crore.
For maintaining public order and managing potentially volatile gatherings, 20 water cannons, each with a capacity of 10,000 litres, will be procured at a cost of Tk128 crore.
The proposal also includes 20 crowd-control vehicles at a cost of Tk220 crore and 15 SWAT vans at Tk187 crore for specialised police units and bomb disposal teams.
Another 100 specialised patrol cars will be purchased at a cost of Tk56 crore to facilitate rapid operations during emergencies.
For the safe transportation of arrested individuals, the project proposes procuring 13 specialised vans at a cost of Tk43 crore. In addition, 55 prison vans will be purchased at Tk33 crore to transport detainees between police stations, courts and prisons.
To strengthen patrols and operations in remote and difficult-to-access areas, the project includes 50 all-terrain vehicles (ATVs) and 100 hill motorcycles for use in hilly regions.
Another 200 high-speed motorcycles will be procured at an estimated cost of Tk160 crore.
The project also includes 50 utility terrain vehicles at a cost of Tk55 crore to transport police-trained dogs.
For intelligence operations and field-level information gathering, six mobile surveillance vehicles will be purchased at a cost of Tk114 crore.
To strengthen police operations in riverine and coastal areas, 15 quick-response boats or speedboats will be procured at a cost of Tk150 crore. Another 15 rescue boats will be purchased to help rescue people stranded in water or involved in accidents.
The proposed specialised fleet also includes 105 commander's suburban vehicles for the transportation of field-level unit commanders, 80 freezer vans for transporting bodies and 80 small deployment utility vehicles for police personnel deployed during elections, religious festivals and public gatherings.
In addition, 10 specialised vehicles will be procured to transport horses used in police ceremonial activities and training.
The two projects do not focus solely on purchasing vehicles. They also place emphasis on ensuring their proper operation, repair and maintenance through specialised training for police personnel.
Under the operational vehicles project, 650 personnel will receive training in light vehicle driving and mechanics, while 300 will be trained in heavy vehicle driving and mechanics. Another 50 personnel will receive training in vehicle repair.
Under the specialised vehicles project, 910 personnel will receive training in driving and mechanics, while another 50 will receive specialised mechanical training.
The operational vehicles project also proposes allocating Tk1.5 crore for purchasing equipment and machinery required for vehicle maintenance and repair.
Home Secretary Manzur Morshed Chowdhury told reporters that some specialised vehicles were also being procured for police personnel who would participate in United Nations peacekeeping missions.
He said the United Nations would reimburse the expenditure incurred for those vehicles at a later stage.
Officials concerned said rapid communication, necessary equipment and appropriate vehicles for different situations were essential to modern policing.
With specialised vehicles, police will be better equipped to overcome the limitations of conventional patrol cars and respond more quickly to emergencies in remote areas and along river routes.
The use of mobile command centres to coordinate the activities of different field units, along with specialised vehicles for crime-scene inspections, is also expected to make investigations more efficient.
The addition of rescue boats will further strengthen the police force's ability to assist people during floods, waterway accidents and other emergencies.
Officials expect the initiative to significantly reduce the police force's vehicle shortage once the projects are implemented. This, in turn, is expected to improve police services across the country, strengthen crime prevention, ensure faster responses to emergencies and enhance public safety.
